official.deadline_note: The programme application at universityadmissions.se closes the same day, 15 January 2027; required documents are due by the document submission deadline (2 February per the scholarship page, 1 February per the how-to-apply page) and the SEK 900 application fee, for which there are no waivers, must be paid by that date.
official.application_cycle: Studies starting August 2027; universityadmissions.se application opens 16 October 2026 and the scholarship application opens 1 December 2026
official.status_note: For the next intake the scholarship application opens 1 December 2026 and closes 15 January 2027; scholarship results are announced 1 April 2027 together with admission results.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The KTH Scholarship covers the tuition fee at KTH for the first and the second year, provided that the study results during the first year are satisfactory.
official.funding_period: full tuition fee, one or two year programme
benefits: The KTH Scholarship covers the full tuition fee of a one or two year master's programme at KTH.
Covers the tuition fee for the first and the second year, provided that the study results during the first year are satisfactory.
No additional documents are required for the scholarship application.
eligibility: Fee-paying student - applicants who are not citizens of the EU, EEA or Switzerland are generally required to pay tuition fees.
Must have applied for a master's programme at KTH as first priority via universityadmissions.se and paid the application fee.
Cannot apply for or be awarded a scholarship for programmes listed as second, third or fourth priority.
Only applicants who fulfil the admission requirements of the programme applied for are eligible for a scholarship.
Academic qualifications from an internationally recognised university equivalent to a Swedish bachelor's degree (final-year students may apply).
English proficiency equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6 / English Level 2.
requirements: Meeting the admission (entry) requirements of the chosen master's programme.
English proficiency equivalent to English 6 / English Level 2.
Required documents for the programme submitted by the document submission deadline in early February.
Payment of the SEK 900 application fee by the document deadline.
documents: No additional documents are required for the scholarship application; the documents submitted with the universityadmissions.se application are used for evaluation.
Documents required by the chosen programme, listed on KTH's Entry requirements page and per University Admissions' country-specific instructions.
Proof of citizenship, for example a copy of the passport, if not required to pay the fee.
selection_criteria: The ranking of the university that awarded the applicant's bachelor's degree.
The applicant's extracurricular research experiences or publications, relevant work experience, relevant teaching experience, awards from competitions and extracurricular activities.
The applicant's motivation regarding how they will contribute to the sustainable development goals with a master's degree from KTH.
coverage: Tuition fee at KTH for the first and the second year of a one or two year master's programme, provided first-year study results are satisfactory.
The full tuition fee for most two-year programmes with both years spent at KTH is SEK 385,000, but it varies between the programmes.
The scholarship does not include living costs.
application_method: First apply for a master's programme at KTH via universityadmissions.se.
When the scholarship application is open, submit the scholarship application using the form on the KTH Scholarship page.
No additional documents are required for the scholarship application.
official.application_route: Apply to a first-priority KTH master's programme at universityadmissions.se, then submit the KTH Scholarship form on the scholarship page between 1 December and 15 January.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to fee-paying students; applicants who are not citizens of the EU, EEA or Switzerland are generally required to pay application and tuition fees, with some exceptions.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - open to fee-paying (non-EU/EEA/Swiss) applicants of all nationalities, with no country list or quota.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No subject restriction, but the programme must be eligible: all master's programmes with two years spent at KTH, the joint programmes Molecular Techniques in Life Science and Biostatistics and Data Science, and the one-year Architectural Lighting Design. Not available to joint Erasmus+ and EIT programmes or Computer Simulations for Science and Engineering; some of those route to the KTH Joint Programme Scholarship.
official.duration: One or two years depending on programme; the scholarship covers the first and the second year.
official.description: The KTH Scholarship covers the full tuition fee of a one or two year master's programme. In 2026, 9 % of the scholarship applicants admitted to a programme were nominated for the KTH Scholarship (65 out of 718). The selection process for the scholarship focuses on academic excellence and drive to contribute to sustainable development.
official.english_requirement: English proficiency equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6 / English Level 2, for example an overall IELTS score of 6.5 or a TOEFL score of 4.5; depending on country of previous studies the requirement can also be met through completed upper secondary or university studies.

not_confirmed: travel_coverage - no travel, installation or insurance allowance is published; the page states only that living costs are not included
per-programme tuition fee - KTH states the fee varies between programmes; SEK 385,000 is the published full fee for most two-year programmes with both years at KTH
verification.notes: All figures and dates taken from KTH's own pages (scholarship page updated 23 Sep 2026, fees page 2 Sep 2026, entry-requirements and how-to-apply pages, cost-of-living page 7 Sep 2026); the 15 January scholarship deadline matches the universityadmissions.se application deadline.

applicant_utility.summary: The KTH Scholarship wipes the full tuition bill - SEK 385,000 for most two-year programmes - but it explicitly excludes living costs, so Stockholm expenses of roughly SEK 7,850-13,000 per month (KTH's 2026 student budget examples) must be covered elsewhere. It cannot be applied for in isolation: it is a short extra step after your universityadmissions.se application and only counts if the KTH programme is ranked first. With just 9 % of admitted applicants nominated in 2026 (65 of 718), treat the scholarship form as a concise motivation pitch built on grades, university standing and a concrete sustainable-development contribution story rather than another bureaucratic hurdle.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA applicants with strong grades from a well-ranked university who place a two-year KTH taught master's first and can self-fund Stockholm living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the universityadmissions.se application with your first-priority KTH programme before 15 January 2027 (application opens 16 October 2026).
Pay the SEK 900 application fee, for which there are no waivers, before the early-February document deadline.
Upload every programme-specific document to universityadmissions.se by the deadline - the scholarship panel evaluates exactly this file.
Check your programme's own KTH fee page to see the real SEK value of the waiver for that programme.
Final-year students: prepare the remaining-credits documentation University Admissions requires.
common_rejection_risks: Ranking the KTH programme second, third or fourth - no scholarship can be awarded below first priority.
Applying under this scholarship to an excluded joint programme (Erasmus+ / EIT / Computer Simulations for Science and Engineering) instead of the KTH Joint Programme Scholarship.
Missing the programme's admission requirements - only admitted applicants are nominated, so a weak file eliminates the scholarship automatically.
Late documents or an unpaid SEK 900 fee by the early-February deadline, which invalidates both admission and nomination.
A generic sustainability statement - motivation on contributing to the sustainable development goals is a scored criterion, not a formality.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Stockholm plus the SEK 900 application fee: KTH's 2026 student budget examples run SEK 7,850-13,000 per month (housing, food, transport, hobbies), and one-off costs such as housing deposits, settling-in items and Swedish residence-permit financial requirements remain with the applicant.
document_audit: The scholarship form itself takes no uploads - every document comes from your universityadmissions.se application, so errors there directly cost you the award.
University Admissions' country-specific rules on translations and certified copies apply; incomplete files are the classic failure point.
English evidence must reach the English 6 level (IELTS 6.5 overall or TOEFL 4.5 is KTH's example); check whether your previous studies exempt you from a test.
Fee status matters: EU/EEA/Swiss citizens fall outside the scholarship because they do not pay tuition.
alerts: The scholarship window is short and fixed: 1 December 2026 to 15 January 2027 for the August 2027 intake.
Second-year coverage is conditional on satisfactory first-year study results - the waiver can stop after year one.
Only 9 % (65 of 718) of admitted applicants were nominated in 2026, and the 2026 master's admission acceptance rate averaged 31 %, so back up this plan with other funding.
Skim the excluded-programme list before committing to an EIT/Erasmus+ or Computer Simulations for Science and Engineering programme - those route to the KTH Joint Programme Scholarship instead.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Two-stage: apply to your first-priority KTH programme at universityadmissions.se by 15 January, upload documents and pay the SEK 900 fee by early February, then file KTH's scholarship form when it opens on 1 December; results follow with admissions on 1 April.
